prompt: My MacBook Air only supports one external monitor, but I want a screen on each side of it when I travel. What should I get?

turns.prompt: My MacBook Air only supports one external monitor, but I want a screen on each side of it when I travel. What should I get?
turns.answer:
What you want is a three-screen portable workstation: your MacBook Air in the middle, with one monitor on the left and another on the right.

For your situation, I would look at a dual-screen laptop extender rather than buying two separate monitors.

There is one important technical requirement: because your MacBook Air supports only one external display natively, the setup needs DisplayLink compatibility to run two independent external screens while keeping the MacBook's own screen open. A regular USB-C splitter won't do this.

My choice: The INVZI Trio Go 16 if you want everything integrated into one portable workstation. The OWC solution if you prefer flexibility in positioning your two monitors.

One caveat: DisplayLink requires installing software and granting macOS permissions. It is great for office work, coding, browsing, and spreadsheets, but less ideal for gaming or protected streaming video.
